labelChirho: carry away, take away, lead off
descriptionChirho: To carry away, transport, or lead off from one place to another. Covers the full range of NT uses: (1) the angel carrying John away in the Spirit to see Babylon and the New Jerusalem (Rev 17:3, 21:10), (2) soldiers leading Jesus away to Pilate (Mark 15:1), (3) angels carrying Lazarus to Abraham's bosom (Luke 16:22), (4) Paul's handkerchiefs and aprons being carried from his body to the sick (Acts 19:12), and (5) approved persons carrying the Corinthian collection to Jerusalem (1 Cor 16:3). Cross-linguistically uniform across active and passive voices: Ger 'wegtragen,' Fra 'emporter,' Spa 'llevar,' Arb 'hamalani/akhadhuhu' (carried me/took him), Heb 'nasa'ani/holikh/huval' (carried/led/was-brought), Kor 'deryeogatda/kkeulgo-gaseo/unbandoeotda' (took away/dragged off/was carried), Hin 'le-gaya/le-jaya-gaya.' All occurrences share the single core meaning of conveyance or transport, with active, passive, and middle forms being purely voice-driven rather than semantically distinct.
